ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, point A is inside circle $O$ with a radius of 5, and $OA = \sqrt{3}$. Let P be a moving point on circle $O$. When $\angle OPA$ reaches its maximum value, what is the length of PA?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure:\\
$\because$ OA and OP are constants,\\
$\therefore$ when PA $\perp$ OA, $\angle$OPA is the maximum,\\
In the right-angled triangle OPA, OA $= \sqrt{3}$, OP $= 5$,\\
$\therefore$ PA $= \sqrt{OP^2 - OA^2}$ $= \boxed{\sqrt{22}}$.

method.method_draft: Use a sine-rule extremum in triangle OPA. First read the diagram as a circle centered at O, with A inside the circle to the right of O, P on the circle, and segments OP, OA, PA forming triangle OPA. From the text, take OP=5 because it is a radius, and OA=√3. Let α=∠OAP and θ=∠OPA. By the sine rule, OA/sin θ = OP/sin α, so sin θ = (OA/OP) sin α = (√3/5) sin α. Since OA is the shortest side, θ is acute, so maximizing θ is equivalent to maximizing sin θ. This occurs when sin α=1, i.e. ∠OAP=90°, so PA ⟂ OA. Then triangle OPA is right-angled at A, and PA=√(OP^2−OA^2)=√(25−3)=√22.
